reasoning_traces.think:
The study examines how defensive pressure alters collective player dynamics in basketball. By applying approximate entropy to track positions, we quantify the regularity of movement patterns. Lower entropy signifies predictable, coordinated behavior, while higher entropy reflects chaotic responses to pressure. Relative phase analysis reveals coordination modes—synchronization versus alternation—in lateral and longitudinal displacements. Distance metrics to centroids measure spatial organization. These primitives form a unified framework: high entropy and anti-phase coordination suggest reactive, isolated responses to defense, whereas low entropy and in-phase motion indicate proactive, collective strategy. The empirical finding that full-court pressure increases distance to opponents' centroid yet restores distance to own team centroid implies defenders spread out defensively but maintain tight offensive cohesion, preserving team fluidity.
